title: Speculative acceptor with time-boxed fallthrough and kernel-fit scoring
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: implement a lightweight 'acceptor' stage for speculative decoding that makes an early accept/reject decision within a strict timebox and signals a graceful fallthrough to the safe decoder when confidence is low. The acceptor uses a compact kernel-fit score (runtime kernel latency + attention compatibility) and short-form acceptance metrics (early-token entropy, top-k stability over N tokens, and cache-hit heuristics). This ticket covers design, simulation, prototype integration in the runtime, and an initial canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptor module implemented in runtime with a configurable timebox parameter (default 8ms for fastpath) and kernel-fit scoring exposed via config
Acceptance decision API documented: accept|soft-accept|reject with rationale code (entropy, stability, kernel-mismatch, timeout)
End-to-end tests demonstrating acceptor triggers for >=70% of short inference requests under lab workloads with false-accept rate <=2%
Fallback path (safe decoder) invoked correctly on reject/timeout and preserves per-request trace ids for post-mortem replay
Telemetry emitted for every decision: decision_type, scores, selected_kernel, time_to_decision, fallback_latency, final_output_match_rate
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on key SLIs breach (see rollout plan)
tasks: Design: define kernel-fit score formulation and weightings (latency penalty, attention-compat mismatch, kv-cache compatibility)
Simulate: run offline traces through acceptance heuristics and measure false-accept/latency delta
Runtime: implement modular acceptor interface and integrate into prefill/decode scheduler pipeline
Kernel telemetry: augment kernel selection path with 'compatibility hints' exposed to acceptor
Fallback: implement soft-accept path that allows a partial commit but routes remainder to safe decoder if confidence decays
Testing: unit + integration tests, chaos tests forcing kernel regression and network noise
Canary: instrument canary, configure alerting thresholds, prepare rollback playbook
Docs: update developer runtime docs and add operational runbook
decisions: Prefer time-boxed acceptor (bounded decision latency) over iterative confidence polling to protect latency SLOs
Use a compact kernel-fit score (single float) rather than a high-dimensional model to keep runtime overhead low
Expose soft-accept vs hard-accept to allow graceful degradation rather than immediate abort on marginal cases
tradeoffs: Aggressive acceptance increases throughput and cost savings but risks quality regressions; we target <=2% false-accept initially
Keeping acceptor logic simple reduces CPU overhead but may miss subtle quality signals that a heavier scorer could catch
Timeboxing tightens latency guarantees but may force more fallbacks, temporarily increasing tail latency on the safe decoder
telemetry_metrics: false_accept_rate (compare acceptor output vs safe-decoder reference on sampled requests)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit/integration tests in CI (no traffic)
Stage 1: internal shadowing mode for 48h against production traffic with no routing changes; collect metrics and sample golden comparisons
Stage 2: 1% canary traffic for 24h with alerting on false_accept_rate>3% or p99 latency growth >10%
Stage 3: 5% canary for 72h with extended regression tests and SLO checks
Stage 4: gradual ramp to 25% then 50% with monitoring; full rollout only after 7 days stable at 50%
Rollback triggers: false_accept_rate spike, >5% increase in tail latency, or regression in downstream user-facing metric from product dashboard
notes: Prototype research found kernel-fit strongly correlates with decode stability on models with custom attention kernels (esp. long-context variants)
We should collaborate with kernel-engineering to define a compact compatibility hint interface (enum + float)
Consider exposing per-tenant tuning flags (timebox and aggressiveness) for Dedicated customers later
